Looking at this question, I need to consider the role of TRAF3 in NF-κB signaling and what happens when it is lost in diffuse large B cell lymphoma (DLBCL).

TRAF3 is a negative regulator of the canonical NF-κB signaling pathway. When TRAF3 function is lost in DLBCL cells, the canonical NF-κB pathway becomes constitutively activated.

In the context of B cell lymphomagenesis and TRAF3 loss:
- The canonical NF-κB pathway is dysregulated
- c-Rel is a key effector subunit in the canonical pathway
- c-Rel is particularly important in B cell malignancies and is a hallmark of constitutive NF-κB activation in these cells
- Research on TRAF3-deficient DLBCL has demonstrated that c-Rel specifically shows enriched nuclear expression, reflecting the constitutive activation of the canonical NF-κB pathway

While p65/RelA and p50 are also part of the canonical pathway, c-Rel is the subunit that is specifically and notably enriched in the nucleus in TRAF3 loss of function DLBCL cells, as it serves as a critical transcription factor driving B cell survival and proliferation in this context.

[ANSWER]E[/ANSWER]
